tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.commands.doc:
Every contributed panel as a palette command.

Names are deduplicated case-insensitively, matching the registry's own
rule, so one panel cannot appear twice in the palette.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.commands.summary: Every contributed panel as a palette command.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.commands.why: Every contributed panel as a palette command.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.commands.roleNote: Dedupes case-insensitively, the same rule PanelRegistry uses.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.commands.title: PanelHost.commands

tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.openByName.name: openByName
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.openByName.summary: Look a panel up by command name and open it.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.openByName.why: Look a panel up by command name and open it.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.openByName.roleNote: Reached only after a built-in and the Harness registry both decline the name, so a panel can never shadow them.

tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.open.name: open
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.open.doc: Show a panel's rows, with the cursor on `select` when it survives.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.open.summary: Show a panel's rows, with the cursor on `select` when it survives.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.open.why: Show a panel's rows, with the cursor on `select` when it survives.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.open.roleNote: Opening is the refresh: plugins are never polled, only asked again after each action.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.open.title: PanelHost.open

tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.activate.name: activate
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.activate.doc:
`enter` on a panel row: run it, then raise any secret it asks for.

The action may toggle state and return nothing, in which case the rows are
simply re-read; or it may return a {@link TuiPanelSecret}, in which case
the prompt is raised, the trimmed answer submitted, and the rows re-read.
A throw — from the action or from `submit` — is reported and the panel
stays open, so a failed toggle never costs the user the panel.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.activate.summary: `enter` on a panel row: run it, then raise any secret it asks for.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.activate.why: `enter` on a panel row: run it, then raise any secret it asks for.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.activate.roleNote: The seam's centre: run the row, optionally prompt and submit, then re-read the rows. A failure is reported and the panel stays open.
tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.activate.title: PanelHost.activate

tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.show.doc: Read the panel's rows and hand them to the surface.

tui/panel-host.ts#PanelHost.show.why: Read the panel's rows and hand them to the surface.

credits.ts::class:PlanCache.name: PlanCache
credits.ts::class:PlanCache.doc:
A brief memory of the last {@link collectPlans} result, so reopening
`/usage` twice in a minute answers from the earlier reading instead of
re-asking every provider.

Pure with an injected clock, so the boundary behaviour is testable. Failures
are cached on the same terms as successes: a provider that just refused or
timed out should not be hammered because the user re-opened the pane, and a
minute is short enough to retry soon anyway. There is deliberately no
invalidation hook tied to sign-in: a fresh credential is exactly the case
where waiting out a minute is preferable to another probe storm.

file-index.ts::class:FileIndex.name: FileIndex
file-index.ts::class:FileIndex.doc: One workspace's file list, recomputed lazily on demand.

index.ts::class:TuiApp.name: TuiApp
index.ts::class:TuiApp.doc: The app: owns the screen, the sessions, and every piece of mutable state.

presence.ts::class:PresencePublisher.name: PresencePublisher
presence.ts::class:PresencePublisher.doc:
Writes and refreshes this device's presence records.

The publisher is deliberately forgiving: a read-only or missing home must
degrade to publishing nothing, never to failing a turn. The overview is a
convenience, and a device that cannot publish simply does not appear.

tui/atfile.ts::class:AtMenu.name: AtMenu
tui/atfile.ts::class:AtMenu.doc:
The inline completion menu over the active `@` token.

It follows the composer rather than owning the keyboard: typing keeps
filtering, `↑`/`↓` (or ctrl+p/n) move, `tab`/`enter` accept, `esc` dismisses
— and only the menu closes, not anything layered beneath it.

tui/fleet.ts::class:FleetView.name: FleetView
tui/fleet.ts::class:FleetView.doc:
The overview's interaction state: what was collected, and where the cursor is.

Kept beside the renderer because it is the same concern and equally pure —
it never reads a file or a socket. The app owns collection and hands the
result here.

tui/panel-host.ts::class:PanelHost.name: PanelHost
tui/panel-host.ts::class:PanelHost.doc:
The host adapter at the panel seam.

It holds the one active panel and never polls a plugin: rows are read when
the panel opens and again after each action, so the redraw *is* the refresh.
Every failure becomes a status line rather than an escaping throw, and the
panel is left open so the row can be tried again.

tui/panels.ts::class:ApprovalPanel.name: ApprovalPanel
tui/panels.ts::class:ApprovalPanel.doc:
One pending tool approval.

There is no persistent grant in the protocol — "allow once" or deny — so the
panel offers exactly those two rows and no "always" temptation.

tui/panels.ts::class:QuestionsPanel.name: QuestionsPanel
tui/panels.ts::class:QuestionsPanel.doc:
The `ask_user_question` flow, question by question.

Single-select answers on `enter`; multi-select toggles with `space` and
collects with `enter`; `tab` moves to the free-text line, and typing on an
option row combines that option's label with the text, the way a form does.
A plan review is the same shape with a markdown body and an approve label
named by the protocol — approval never carries feedback, because the
protocol reads feedback as "keep planning".

tui/panels.ts::class:LoginPanel.name: LoginPanel
tui/panels.ts::class:LoginPanel.doc:
One running `ctx.authorization` attempt, surfaced as a panel.

Deliberately thin: this tracks only what is on screen — the last notice,
the live prompt if one is waiting, and what has been typed or highlighted
for it. Resolving a prompt is the caller's job, the same split
{@link ApprovalPanel} and {@link QuestionsPanel} keep, because answering one
is a call into the Harness and this module may depend on nothing from it.

tui/screen.ts::class:Screen.name: Screen
tui/screen.ts::class:Screen.doc:
Owns stdin/stdout for the lifetime of the app. Construction does not touch
the terminal; {@link Screen.start} does, and {@link Screen.stop} is safe to
call more than once so teardown paths can be blunt.

tui/state.ts::class:Composer.name: Composer
tui/state.ts::class:Composer.doc:
The composer. A plain multi-line buffer with a cursor, wide enough in
behavior to feel like an editor: word motion, line motion, and kill-to-end.

tui/state.ts::class:InputHistory.name: InputHistory
tui/state.ts::class:InputHistory.doc:
Recall of previously sent prompts, the way a shell recalls its history.

`recall` walks older (`-1`) or newer (`+1`) entries and returns the text to
show, or `undefined` when there is nothing further in that direction — the
caller then falls back to ordinary cursor motion. The draft being typed is
remembered the first time recall leaves it, so walking back down to the end
restores it rather than stranding the user on the last sent prompt.

tui/state.ts::class:Palette.name: Palette
tui/state.ts::class:Palette.doc: The popup that filters slash commands as they are typed.

tui/state.ts::class:Picker.name: Picker
tui/state.ts::class:Picker.doc:
The full-pane list that replaces the transcript for `/resume` and `/model`.

It filters as you type and, when grouped, prints a header each time the
subtitle changes — so a model list reads provider by provider rather than as
one undifferentiated column.

tui/usage-view.ts::class:UsageView.name: UsageView
tui/usage-view.ts::class:UsageView.doc: The pane's own state: whether it is open, and the data it last drew.

tui/vim.ts::class:Vim.name: Vim
tui/vim.ts::class:Vim.doc:
Modal vim state over one composer.

Insert mode is the default: enabling vim must not change what typing does.
An operator key (`d`) waits for its motion, and any key that is not a valid
continuation cancels it — vim's own rule, and the safe one for a draft.

tui-host-core.ts::class:ShortcutRegistry.name: ShortcutRegistry
tui-host-core.ts::class:ShortcutRegistry.doc: Shortcut claims, without any Cordis dependency — the testable half.

tui-host-core.ts::class:StatusLine.name: StatusLine
tui-host-core.ts::class:StatusLine.doc: The one-line status slot, also independent of Cordis.

tui-host-core.ts::class:PanelRegistry.name: PanelRegistry
tui-host-core.ts::class:PanelRegistry.doc: Contributed panels, keyed by lowercased command name.

tui-host.ts::class:TuiHost.name: TuiHost
tui-host.ts::class:TuiHost.doc:
The extension seam (`ctx.tuiHost`). Plugins register shortcuts and a status
line; the app dispatches keys and draws the line, and owns nothing else.
